headline: Tolle dominates as Red Sox bats finally wake up in Chicago
morning_brew: That is the kind of performance we have been begging to see all summer. Payton Tolle was absolutely locked in on Tuesday night, carving up the White Sox for six shutout innings and only giving up two hits. When you lose a guy like Ranger Suarez to injury, you need someone else to step up and stop the bleeding, and Tolle answered the call with six strikeouts and command that looked like a vet out there on the mound.

The offense finally gave our pitchers some breathing room too. Andruw Monasterio and Ceddanne Rafaela provided the pop with their homers, and the team combined for eleven hits to secure a dominant 8-1 victory. It was a complete game from top to bottom, the kind of win that makes you feel like the team actually has a heartbeat again. Watching them put up four runs in the ninth just to pour it on was the perfect way to end the night.

My mother watched the highlights this morning and said 'it is about time they played like they wanted it,' and for once, she is right. We cannot get ahead of ourselves with a 41-48 record, but taking the first game against Chicago is a start. Elsewhere, the C's are still sorting through the aftermath of the Jaylen Brown trade, and Jayson Tatum's comments about the partnership ending just remind me that we are in for a long, quiet offseason on Causeway Street.

news_digest.headline: Tatum: 'Tough' to see Brown go, proud of 'great years' together
news_digest.dans_take: It is painful to hear JT talk about it because we all know that duo should have had more time together.

news_digest.headline: Contreras, Ashcraft, Luzardo among All-Star Game replacements
news_digest.dans_take: Good for Willson Contreras, he has been a bright spot in this lineup all season.

trend_watch.trend: Six innings, two hits, six strikeouts
trend_watch.dans_take: That was his best stuff all year. If he keeps dealing like that, the rotation isn't as hopeless as I thought.
The man found his swing at the perfect time. We need that kind of production from the middle of the order.
He has been playing with a ton of energy, and seeing him drive the ball like that is a great sign.
